title: Older Americans Month Community BINGO Challenge
source_title: Kramer Elementary | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content: Every May, Older Americans Month recognizes the contributions of older adults, highlights aging trends, and reaffirms commitments to serve our older community members. The 2026 theme is “Champion Your Health”.Throughout the month of May, Oxford Seniors, Age-Friendly Oxford, and the Coalition for a Healthy Community, Oxford Area are partnering to highlight and offer programming focused on promoting physical, mental, and emotional health and well-being at all ages.You can participate by playing “Community BINGO” with us! It’s as easy as 1, 2, 3!1) Print your own or pick up a Community Bingo card at any of the following locations:Oxford Seniors, 922 Tollgate Dr., OxfordOxford Lane Library, 441 S. Locust St.The Knolls of Oxford, Clubhouse or Front DeskScripps Gerontology Center, 396 Upham Hall, on campus2) Every time you do something listed on the card, mark it off. The goal is to get “BINGO” as many times as possible. A “BINGO” is marking off any 5 squares in a straight line – either vertically, horizontally, or diagonally.3) Bring your completed BINGO card to the Intergenerational BINGO Party on Sun. May 31 from 3:00 – 5:00 p.m. at Oxford Seniors for prizes, snacks, and FUN! A PDF version of the BINGO card is attached if you'd like to print one at home.

summary: **Older Americans Month** celebrates older adults' contributions throughout May 2026 with the theme "Champion Your Health." Oxford Seniors, Age-Friendly Oxford, and the Coalition for a Healthy Community are hosting **Community BINGO** to promote physical, mental, and emotional health. Pick up a BINGO card at Oxford Seniors (922 Tollgate Dr.), Oxford Lane Library (441 S. Locust St.), The Knolls of Oxford, or Scripps Gerontology Center (396 Upham Hall), complete activities throughout May, and bring your completed card to the **Intergenerational BINGO Party on May 31, 3:00-5:00 PM** at Oxford Seniors for prizes and snacks.

title: Field Day, No School Days, and Recent Activities
source_title: Kramer Elementary | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content: Happy Friday, Kramer Families!It’s been another busy week of testing, and our 3rd and 5th graders did an amazing job—we’re so proud of their hard work and effort! Our 1st grade students had a wonderful time visiting You’re Fired, where they enjoyed painting ceramic tiles. The 5th graders also had a fun walking field trip to Spring Street Treats for some delicious ice cream. Meanwhile, our Kindergarten students explored and enjoyed their trip to Farbach-Werner Nature Preserve.Field Day is coming up on May 8th! Please see the flyer for more information. We can really use volunteers to help make the day a success. Be sure to sign up using the QR code or the link attached below the flyer. Please remember that ALL parents and guardians must have a background check on file with the board office in order to attend any field trip. This process can take a few days, so we encourage you to plan ahead. Please reach out to the main office if you have any questions.Thank you for your continued support and partnership. We appreciate all you do to help make Kramer such a great place to learn and grow—have a wonderful weekend!NO SCHOOL MONDAY MAY 4TH AND TUESDAY MAY 5TH!

Recent highlights include 3rd and 5th graders completing testing, 1st graders painting ceramic tiles at You're Fired, 5th graders walking to Spring Street Treats for ice cream, and Kindergarteners visiting Farbach-Werner Nature Preserve.

title: Kramer Reading at Home Program Success
source_title: Kramer Elementary | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
Kramer's 

Reading 

at 

Home 

(RAH)

Kramer's Reading at Home (RAH)

This school year, Kramer’s Reading At Home (RAH) program was a huge success, and we are so proud of our students’ dedication to reading!An incredible 82% of our K–2 students participated by turning in at least one reading sheet; that’s 208 young readers building strong habits at home. Even more impressive, almost half of those participants turned in 10 or more sheets, showing consistent commitment throughout the year.Our most avid readers truly went above and beyond. We had 26 students read over 500 books, and our top three readers each surpassed an amazing 1,000 books!Altogether, Kramer students recorded over 39,000 books read this year! Each book read is an opportunity to grow imagination, vocabulary, and a lifelong love of reading.These impressive readers took home more than 1,000 books from the RAH cart, helping them build their own home libraries. Rewards also kept motivation high, with the favorite prize this year being coupons to local businesses like Oxford Doughnut Shoppe and Spring Street Treats.Thank you to our families for supporting reading at home and helping make this program such a meaningful part of our school community. We can’t wait to see even more reading adventures next year!

summary: Kramer's Reading at Home (RAH) program achieved remarkable participation this year, with **82% of K-2 students (208 readers)** turning in at least one reading sheet. Nearly half submitted 10+ sheets, while **26 students read over 500 books** and three students each read more than **1,000 books**. Students collectively recorded **over 39,000 books read** and took home 1,000+ books from the RAH cart. Popular rewards included coupons to Oxford Doughnut Shoppe and Spring Street Treats.
